source: Lee, Song, Yoon, Park, Kang (2025; AAAI 2026) The Curious Case of Analogies: Investigating Analogical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Relation information moves through mid-upper layers when the model answers right. Failures coincide with missing relation information there. Models also often fail to apply a relation they hold to new entities. Patching hidden states at key token positions recovers part of the failures.
numbers: Patching gains (Table 1): Gemma-7B +38.4% (replace first pair, Exp 1) and +38.1% (patch e2 into link, Exp 2); Qwen2.5-14B +35.6% and +30.5%. Probe about 82.9% (layers 20-30, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct). Proportional sets after filtering: Qwen 1,478 correct/1,122 wrong; Gemma 756/997; Llama-2-13B 809/924. Story set: 360 Qs, two options.
limits: The 38.4% belongs to Gemma-7B. No count splits failures into missing vs not applied. No overall accuracy reported. CoT and relation-naming prompts were NOT tested.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: the 38.4% is an internal-edit ceiling, not proof that a prompt can reach it. Whether naming supplies missing relation info cannot be shown from this paper.

source: KnowledgePrompts: knowledge-enhanced prompts for proportional analogies, arXiv 2412.00869v2
finding: Tested zero-shot, 1-shot, 5-shot, structured-knowledge prompts (random or semantic) and a targeted-knowledge prompt (TKP) on about 15K multiple-choice analogies over 236 relation types. TKP states the shared relation and the human reasoning step. It helped 6 of 9 models and hurt 3.
numbers: EMA accuracy zero-shot -> TKP: GPT-3.5-Turbo 45.70 -> 55.25 (+9.55); FlanT5 36.47 -> 44.26 (+7.79); Falcon 24.17 -> 25.40; Mistral 26.59 -> 27.37; CodeT5 20.64 -> 21.64; CodeParrot 0.00 -> 2.09; Zephyr 29.46 -> 15.83 (-13.63); GPT2 22.65 -> 21.64; Orca 24.54 -> 24.20. Structured-knowledge prompts for GPT-3.5: random 38.29, semantic 38.79, both below zero-shot.
limits: TKP bundles the relation name with a reasoning description, so the name alone is not isolated. One hand-written template per prompt type. Relation text given by the experimenter, not self-generated.
agent_relevance: Nearest direct hint for gaps 1-3: stating the relation helped the strongest model by about 10 points, but not specifically as a name and not stably across models. Extra relevant text without the relation did not help, consistent with value coming from the relation, not from tokens.

source: Relational Knowledge Distillation Using Fine-tuned Function Vectors, arXiv 2601.08169
finding: Injecting a fine-tuned relation function vector (a compressed name of the relation in activation space) lifts relation completion and analogy, most on far analogies.
numbers: GPT-J zero-shot relation completion: simple 5.13 -> 87.22%, complex 35.41 -> 63.34%, SemEval 8.83 -> 60.78%. One-shot top-5 analogy, base -> composite FV: Green far GPT-J 42.5 -> 61.0, LLaMa-3.1 57.5 -> 74.0, GPT-2 22.5 -> 44.5, LLaMa-2 60.0 -> 74.5; Green near LLaMa-2 77.5 -> 74.5, LLaMa-3.1 87.5 -> 85.0; SAT LLaMa-3.1 52.7 -> 58.8. ActAdd with label prompts such as Plural: only 18.0-18.5% vs 75.2% for fine-tuned FV.
limits: Four small/mid models, word-pair A:B::C:D only, 5 seeds. Text and table disagree in places (GPT-J far baseline 49% vs 42.5%). BATS overlaps training relations. Near analogies slightly worsen.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: a relation representation helps far analogies more than near ones, the direction we want. It is activation-level; a label token alone (ActAdd) was weak. Prompt-level transfer unknown.

source: Xu et al. (2023) LLMs and the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus: Successes, Failures, and the Importance of Object-based Representations
finding: Giving GPT-4 the objects (extracted and structured) instead of a raw grid raised ARC success. Adding edge/relation info lowered it.
numbers: ARC 50-task subset GPT-4: direct-grid best 13/50 -> object JSON best 23/50. Full 400 training tasks: 81 -> 97. Mini-ARC (149): 35 -> 45. Grid -> object: GPT-3.5 2 -> 6; LLaMA2-13B 0 -> 6; LLaMA2-70B 2 -> 7. Object JSON 21 (few-shot) / 23 (CoT); Object JSON + Edge 19 / 16; Descriptors + Edge 18 / 12. GPT-4V 2/50.
limits: ARC, not ConceptARC (no ConceptARC solve counts given). Objects were extracted by code, not self-named by the model. Edge info was not a clean naming test; authors blame information overload.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: naming entities helps beyond RAVEN (Hu 2023), but adding more relation structure can hurt. Name the few relations that matter, do not dump all.

source: Ye et al. (2024) AnaloBench: Benchmarking the Identification of Abstract and Long-context Analogies
finding: Finding the analogous story among 4 options (T1) falls steeply with story length, and retrieval from a bank of about 200 stories (T2) is near random for most models.
numbers: T1 accuracy at 1 / 10 / 30 sentences: GPT-4 89.1 / 66.5 / 60.7; GPT-3.5 65.3 / 46.4 / 30.8; Claude 68.2 / 30.2 / 25.9; LLaMA2-chat-70B 55.6 / 39.2 / 29.5; Human 96.0 / 72.5 / 73.3; random 25. Seed data: 340 human stories in 47 analogy clusters. T2: GPT-4 and Claude-v2 near the random-retrieval baseline except GPT-4 Turbo on 1-sentence.
limits: No relation-hint or summary-then-retrieve arm. T2 Table 8 not read (truncated). Longer stories are GPT-4 elaborations.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: with long surface-rich stories the far-analogy gap persists and weaker models fall to chance. Supports compressing cases to short relation statements before matching (S2), but this paper does not test it.

source: Jiayang et al. (2023) StoryAnalogy: Deriving Story-level Analogies from Large Language Models
finding: LLMs identify story analogies poorly and their scores do not track entity or relation similarity as humans do. A prompt that says what a creative analogy is (few shared entities, similar relations) helped some models.
numbers: Identification (random 25, human 85.7): FlanT5-xxl 45.0/46.3/45.0 at 0/1/3-shot; GPT-3.5 44.2/34.1/33.1; ChatGPT 35.8/29.2/32.3; LLaMa-65B 27.7/28.6/29.5. Spearman with analogy score: human 62.5; ChatGPT 2.3; GPT-3.5 0.9; FlanT5 4.7; LLaMa 1.2. Template C vs plain A: FlanT5-xxl 48.0 vs 41.2; GPT-3.5 44.0 vs 33.7. More demonstrations: no consistent benefit.
limits: Older models. No CoT arm. Template effect small or absent for LLaMa and ChatGPT.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1-2: telling the model to attend to relations rather than entities lifted two of four models by 7-10 points. This is the nearest prompt-level analogue of a relational label.

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Evaluating the Robustness of Analogical Reasoning in LLMs (appendix and prompt details)
finding: The paper tested no hint, CoT or relation-description arm; it says it did not experiment with non-zero-shot or CoT prompting. Newer GPT-4 snapshots did not beat 0613 on digit matrices.
numbers: Permuted-alphabet successor checks (original / non-original / symbol): GPT-3 1.0/0.82/1.0; GPT-3.5 0.99/0.95/0.94; GPT-4 1.0/1.0/1.0. Predecessor: GPT-3.5 1.0/0.75/0.94; GPT-4 1.0/0.97/1.0. Digit-matrix alternate-blank checks: GPT-3.5 found the blank in 6 of 9, GPT-4 in 9 of 9.
limits: Only 2023-era snapshots. Gap 7 (do label gains survive perturbations) is untested.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open. The models can state the successor rule on permuted alphabets (near 1.0) yet fail the analogy task, so the failure is in applying a known rule. An explicit rule statement before solving may or may not help; untested.

source: Beger, Yi, Fu, Denton, Moskvichev, Tsai, Rajamanickam, Mitchell (2025) Distinguishing Performance From Competence in Evaluations of Humanlike Abstract Reasoning
finding: On ConceptARC, reasoning models match or beat humans on text output accuracy, but their stated rules are less often the intended abstraction. Visually, output accuracy collapses while rules are often right.
numbers: Text pass@1, medium effort: o3 77.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro 66.0, Claude Sonnet 4 60.2 (72.5 after re-assessment); o3 low 68.3. Humans 73%. With Python in text: o3 75.6. Visual medium+Python: o3 29.2, Claude 6.9, Gemini 5.8. About 27% of o3 and Gemini correct-output rules were correct-unintended or incorrect; Claude about 19%; humans about 7%. Visual correct-intended rules vs correct grids: o3 40.0 vs 29.2; Claude 14.4 vs 6.9; Gemini 23.5 vs 5.8.
limits: ConceptARC only, text and visual. Rule grading depends on the authors' annotation. Appendix K percentages not read.
agent_relevance: Gaps 5-6: 2025 reasoning models close the ConceptARC accuracy gap that GPT-4 had in 2023 but often with shortcut rules. A scaffold should check the stated relation, not just the answer. No naming scaffold tested.

source: Mind Melds: redundant labels and between-person alignment, Exp 1 and 2 (re-read in full, gap 8)
finding: Redundant labels during a matching task made later free sorting more similar across people. Categoricality mediated the effect fully in Exp 1 and partly in Exp 2.
numbers: Exp 1 N=129 (Baseline 45, No Labels 43, Labels 41; 39 excluded). Alignment Labels .20 vs Baseline .11 (b=.07, p<.001) and No Labels .12 (b=.10, p<.001). Exp 2 N=122 (41/37/44; 65 excluded): .35 vs .21 (b=.14, p<.001) and .27 (b=.07, p=.02). Categoricality Exp 1: .65 vs .38 (b=.28, p=.024) and .40 (b=.26, p=.038); Exp 2: .66 vs .49 (b=.17, p=.04), vs No Labels .60 ns. Clusters Exp 1: 3.1 vs 4.1 and 3.9; two-cluster sorts 53% vs 33% and 20%.
limits: Heavy exclusions (39 and 65). Unstandardised b only. Diversity not tested directly. Within-category alignment was lower with labels in Exp 1 (more idiosyncratic local sorting) but between-category alignment was higher in Exp 2.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: shared labels raise agreement across people at category level, so shared names may raise agreement across agent samples. Cost to diversity is mixed, not shown. Keep the vocabulary small and fixed per run, and keep an unlabeled sample if diversity matters.

source: Liu & Lupyan (2026) The unity of sense and mind: a review of cross-domain mapping, Psychon. Bull. Rev. 33:25
finding: Proposes four mechanisms for cross-domain mappings: statistical learning, magnitude matching, valence matching, semantic mediation (shared words link domains). Whether language drives or reflects mappings stays unresolved.
numbers: Table 1: 72 studies of cross-sensory mappings; Table 2: 84 cross-conceptual. Dolscheid 2013: Dutch speakers trained to say thick/thin showed Farsi-like thickness-pitch effects. Kreung speakers without spatial pitch words still link pitch to height (Parkinson 2012). Lakens 2012: making negative words more frequent removed the valence-height effect. Flute-as-a-job: 20% teacher vs 7% baseline (Liu & Lupyan 2023).
limits: Read only the first 100k and a reference slice (200k-300k) of a 321k-character page. No LLM discussion found in the read text.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 (part): supports the idea that a shared word can link two domains, relevant to naming a relation to bridge domains, while showing language is not always necessary. No AI conclusion obtained.

source: Lupyan, Gentry & Zettersten (2026) How Important Is Language for Human-Like Intelligence? Perspectives on Psychological Science 21(1):115-120
finding: Abstract only (Europe PMC record; PMID 41499467, not in PMC). Argues language gives compact representations that make abstract concepts easier to reason about, and these are the accumulated product of many minds. Learning language exposes any learner, biological or artificial, to culturally evolved abstractions and a compressed model of conceptual and causal structure.
limits: Paywalled; abstract only. No experiments in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 (part): the current Lupyan stance is that language supplies abstractions, supporting S2 naming in principle. It is a position, not a measured result.

source: Guo et al. (2024) Can Multimodal Large Language Model Think Analogically? arXiv 2411.01307
finding: An MLLM that writes a text description of the entities and the implicit relation, inserted into the prompt of a smaller model, gave modest gains on MARS; fine-tuning LLaVA as predictor gave more.
numbers: MARS Hits@1: MKGformer 30.1 -> 32.4 with explainer; FLAVA 26.4 -> 33.3. Predictor (LLaVA) accuracy 56.20 vs LLaVA base 43.39 and internVL 2 45.69. Implicit relation inference: LLaVA base 25.55, predictor 44.12; explainer variants poor (Hits@1 1.6 vs 0.5). Ablation: 54.4 without mapping module, 24.3 without step-1 tuning. MBARD zero-shot ChatGPT-4 68.0%.
limits: Knowledge-graph analogy with images, multimodal, fine-tuned. Not a clean label test.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1-2: model-written relation text raised a downstream model by 2.3 to 6.9 Hits@1, an example of self-generated relation text helping. Mixed on relation inference.

source: Gap sweep record: direct LLM tests of relation name vs domain tag vs none, name placement, compare-then-name
finding: No paper found that runs Jamrozik-style retrieval (relation label vs domain label vs none) on an LLM, varies name position, or crosses alignment x label for LLMs. Closest are d02 (relation stated in prompt), d06 (relation-focused instruction) and d12 (model-written relation text).
numbers: Search access this session: arXiv search, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned 429 or budget-exhausted; WebSearch gave one result set and then refused. Only direct page fetches worked.
limits: Absence of evidence from a constrained search, not proof of absence. Gaps 1, 2, 3 and 10 therefore remain open.
agent_relevance: The direct test remains the main open item: equal-token relation name vs domain tag vs nothing, before vs after, given vs self-generated.

source: INLG 2025 (2025.inlg-main.28): LLM analogical reasoning is fragile and sensitive to prompt design (search snippet)
finding: A search snippet says analogical reasoning in LLMs is highly sensitive to prompt design. Paper not opened.
agent_relevance: Weak hint that wording of a relation statement may matter. Do not cite without opening.

source: Liu, Marjieh, Zhu, Goldberg, Griffiths (2026) LLMs support the parallelogram theory of analogy (carry-over of c17)
finding: Carried from c17: LLM analogies fit a relation-as-vector model better than human ones. Not re-opened in this gap pass.
agent_relevance: Context for gap 5: relation as a direction is consistent with d03 function vectors.

source: Xu et al. 2023 reasoning-quality audit (from d04)
finding: Correct answers with raw grids were mostly not backed by correct reasoning; with object representations they mostly were.
numbers: 3 of 13 grid solves had correct reasoning; 20 of 23 object solves had correct reasoning.
limits: Small N, manual judging by the authors.
agent_relevance: Supports checking the stated relation rather than accepting answer-only success; matches d08.
